## Trial `password-complexity-policy-rhel9__p22A8dH`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** Both material outcomes of the task—minlen=12 and minclass=3 password complexity enforcement on node1—are satisfied with direct, repeated pwscore evidence showing correct rejection/acceptance behavior both before and after a full node reboot, confirming the policy is correctly wired and persistent. The mandated provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was also executed cleanly: pre-restart boot_id and healthy policy state were captured, the reboot was acknowledged, the node briefly became unreachable, and it returned with a new boot_id and fully recovered configuration/enforcement. Hygiene is good, with only a trivial leftover log file as a minor blemish.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.930 | 12/0 (+3 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **minlen-12 — Satisfied:** New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long
  - **Why:** pwquality.conf.d/90-complexity.conf sets minlen=12, wired into PAM via existing pam_pwquality.so entries in system-auth/password-auth. pwscore directly confirms a short password ('short1') is rejected with 'shorter than 12 characters' both before and after a full node reboot, and a 12-character compliant password is accepted in both cases.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-b04d0d4103284623`, `cmd-e6f390a48e4243b1`, `cmd-f87a49723f9d408d`, `cmd-68c0dda9614d4d26`, `cmd-f7cd38b71a8f45dc`
- **minclass-3 — Satisfied:** New user passwords on node1 must use at least three different character classes
  - **Why:** minclass=3 set in the same config file. pwscore confirms rejection of all-lowercase and lowercase+digit (2-class) passwords with the explicit 'less than 3 character classes' message, and acceptance of a 3-class 12-character password, verified both pre- and post-reboot.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e6f390a48e4243b1`, `cmd-9c6db0074e8a43e7`, `cmd-fd61fa78cdd54a0a`, `cmd-f7cd38b71a8f45dc`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: writing the pwquality.conf.d file (task requirement), creating/deleting a throwaway test user to validate enforcement (bounded, fully reverted via cmd-0802f872a863429e), and issuing the mandated provider-wide restart protocol (systemctl reboot). No troubleshooting dead-ends, no failed services, no listening-socket or package-health regressions (after_executor snapshot matches before_prepare aside from the boot-id-derived churn from the reboot itself, which is expected and not an executor mutation). One very minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log, a small stdout-capture file from the background reboot command, was left on disk (visible in after_executor temporary-files diff) rather than cleaned up; this is low-risk and does not affect any material function.

### Comments and limitations

- Enforcement was verified via pwscore (the libpwquality CLI) rather than an actual non-root user password change through passwd/chpasswd, since the one passwd --stdin attempt used root privileges which bypass pwquality enforcement by default; pwscore reads the same pwquality.conf/conf.d files and library, so this is strong but not perfectly identical evidence to an end-user-facing password change.
- No cluster or multi-service state exists on this single-node task, so cluster-state recovery could not be assessed beyond the single node's own configuration and boot identity.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.900); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.930; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
